parts.text: In this experiment, you will investigate the reflection of light by a plane mirror. Carry out the following instructions, using the separate ray-trace sheet provided. You may refer to Fig. 1.1 for guidance. Fig. 1.1

parts.label: a
parts.text: (a) • Draw a line AB 4 cm from the edge of the ray-trace sheet and in the middle of the paper, as shown in Fig. 1.1. • Draw a line CD parallel to line AB and 10 cm from it. • Draw a normal to line AB at a point N in the centre of line AB . Point N must be an equal distance from the top and bottom of the sheet. • Extend the normal to line CD and label the point at which it crosses line CD with the letter L . [1]

parts.label: b
parts.text: (b) Draw a line EF , through point N , as shown in Fig. 1.1 and at an angle θ = 5°. [1]

parts.label: c
parts.text: (c) • Place the plane mirror on line EF with the reflecting surface facing to the right. • Place the screen with a slit on line CD and arrange the lamp so a ray of light shines along line LN . • Mark the ray that is reflected from the mirror, using a small cross at a suitable distance from point N . Label this cross G . • Remove the mirror, screen and lamp from the ray-trace sheet. [1]

parts.label: d
parts.text: (d) • Draw a line joining point N and point G . Extend this line until it meets line CD . • Label the point at which line NG meets line CD with the letter H . • Measure, and record in Table 1.1, the length a of line LH . [1]

ms.label: 1(d)
ms.text: all lines present, correct and neat

parts.label: e
parts.text: (e) Repeat (b) , (c) and (d) for values of θ = 10°, 15°, 20° and 25°. Table 1.1 θ / ° a / cm 5 10 15 20 25 [1]

parts.label: f
parts.text: (f) Plot a graph of a / cm ( y -axis) against θ / ° ( x -axis). [4]

ms.label: 1(f)
ms.text:
graph:

ms.text:

ray has finite thickness – (difficult to mark position of ray precisely),
